comments.title: An OFFSET overflowing an int counts as an unrepresentable page: 400
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.60 — An OFFSET overflowing an int counts as an unrepresentable page: 400

**Not taken:** answer 200 with an empty page for any int page past the end

**Why:** the spec says unrepresentable pages are 400 and past-the-end pages are 200 — it never says where one ends. Hibernate fails on an offset over Integer.MAX_VALUE, so that is where I drew it; a human could equally read "unrepresentable" as "not an int".

comments.title: Sort tokens are strictly lowercase: `name,ASC` is a 400
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.70 — Sort tokens are strictly lowercase: `name,ASC` is a 400

**Not taken:** accept any case, as Spring's Direction.fromString does

**Why:** the spec lists exactly four accepted values and rejects everything else. Lenient case would be friendlier and nobody asked for strictness, which keeps this below 0.8.

comments.title: An empty `sort=` / `size=` / `page=` means "omitted", not malformed
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.65 — An empty `sort=` / `size=` / `page=` means "omitted", not malformed

**Not taken:** reject an empty value with 400

**Why:** Spring's defaultValue applies to empty strings and the old `lastName=` already worked that way. The spec only defines omitted parameters, so empty is my call.

comments.title: The service sends only the parameters it is given; the grid always sends all four
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.80 — The service sends only the parameters it is given; the grid always sends all four

**Not taken:** the service fills in defaults itself

**Why:** the defaults live on the server, so a bare `getOwners()` matches a bare GET. The grid sends its full state anyway, so the server defaults never decide what the screen shows.

comments.title: Add Owner is always shown, not only after the first load
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.75 — Add Owner is always shown, not only after the first load

**Not taken:** keep it gated on the first successful load, as before

**Why:** the spec wants Add Owner available across loading, empty and error. The old gate hid it on a failed load, so keeping it would contradict that.

comments.title: A non-empty total with an empty page shows an empty table plus paginator
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.70 — A non-empty total with an empty page shows an empty table plus paginator

**Not taken:** jump back to the last valid page automatically

**Why:** the spec only forbids claiming "no matches" and asks that navigation back stay available. An automatic jump would send a second request nobody triggered.

comments.title: V4 copied byte-for-byte from `origin/db27oct`, so the index name differs from the design
comments.anchor: CREATE INDEX owners_last_name_prefix_idx ON owners (last_name text_pattern_ops);
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.50 — V4 copied byte-for-byte from `origin/db27oct`, so the index name differs from the design

**Not taken:** my own V4 with comments and the name `owners_last_name_pattern_idx`

**Why:** a database that ran db27oct would otherwise fail Flyway checksum validation on boot. Whether db27oct was ever deployed is unknown to me, and this checkout's dev DB holds a third V4 that matches neither.

comments.title: Malformed typed params get a 400 on every REST endpoint
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.65 — Malformed typed params get a 400 on every REST endpoint

**Not taken:** validate `page`/`size` as strings inside the owner list only

**Why:** the global advice already owns REST error mapping per the style rules, and 400 is right for any bad client value. It does change the error code of `/api/owners/abc` from 500 to 400, which the spec calls an unchanged contract.

comments.title: Material's default "Items per page" label, not the sketch's "Rows per page"
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.60 — Material's default "Items per page" label, not the sketch's "Rows per page"

**Not taken:** a MatPaginatorIntl provider relabelling it "Rows per page"

**Why:** the proposal calls its sketch illustrative, not final, so I avoided a custom provider. A product owner may still want the sketch's wording.

comments.title: End-to-end traversal checks the UI against the API's own order
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.70 — End-to-end traversal checks the UI against the API's own order

**Not taken:** hard-code the seeded order of all 26 owners in the feature

**Why:** other specs leave owners behind in a shared DB, so a fixed list would break on reruns. The backend tests are the independent oracle for the order itself; the e2e test proves the UI pages through it without gaps.
